CONDITIONAL: QA1 static audit, sprint 1, round 1. Verdict CONDITIONAL.
Audited commit 684df01, tree e520590ba221fcadcbac42bb2a95190735914d39, working tree clean.
Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before recording; unchanged from earlier read this session.

VERIFIED CLEAN
- Req 1: Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 at repo root. OK.
- Req 2: typecheck clean (tsc --noEmit), lint clean (eslint, exit 0), next build exit 0, both routes prerendered static. No `any` in lib/types.ts. OK.
- Req 3: Vitest 4.1.10 wired, 1/1 passing. OK.
- Req 4: all ten named types declared and exported in lib/types.ts, each with a doc comment. No domain type declared anywhere else in the diff (grepped every .ts/.tsx/.mts changed). OK.
- Req 5: CaseExcerpt.verifiedBy / .verifiedDate / .sourceUrl all non-optional. OK.
- Req 6: disclaimer rendered once from root layout (app/layout.tsx:28), not per-page. Exact wording in DisclaimerBanner.tsx, exported as DISCLAIMER_TEXT and covered by a character-for-character test. OK.
- Req 9: two routes exist (/ and /about), both build. OK.
- AC 4: build/lint/typecheck/test scripts all present in package.json. OK.

REQUIRED FIXES (all must be addressed before re-audit)

1. [HIGH] CodeGround.ground is an unconstrained string -- lib/types.ts:58.
   ConcernCategory two declarations above is a tight union; the BC Human Rights Code
   grounds are likewise a closed list. The doc comment says 'e.g. "disability",
   "family status", "sex", "age"' -- the value set was known and left open.
   CaseExcerpt.groundTags (lib/types.ts:96) is also string[], so Sprint 4's matcher
   joins two unconstrained string spaces. "disability" vs "Disability" vs "physical
   disability" compiles and matches nothing; zero matches on a triage tool is
   indistinguishable from "no issue found". Make it a union type.

2. [HIGH] CaseExcerpt.isPlaceholder is optional -- lib/types.ts:109.
   Provenance fields are correctly required, then the one flag answering "is this
   citation real?" is optional. undefined is falsy, so a record that omits it defaults
   to looking verified -- the inverse of the safe default, on the exact failure mode
   CLAUDE.md documents this project already hitting once (the hallucinated
   Devine v. British Columbia, 2022 BCHRT 45). Make it required.

3. [MEDIUM] IssueGuide can represent a contradictory state -- lib/types.ts:151,158.
   matches: MatchResult[] and casesWithheld: boolean are independent, so
   casesWithheld: true alongside a populated matches array compiles -- precisely the
   state the citation guard exists to prevent. The line 155 doc comment asserts an
   invariant the type does not enforce. Use a discriminated union so the bad state
   will not compile. Same principle req 5 already applies to CaseExcerpt provenance.

4. [MEDIUM] Dark-mode legibility -- app/globals.css:18-22 vs app/page.tsx, app/about/page.tsx.
   globals.css flips --background to #0a0a0a under prefers-color-scheme: dark, but both
   page bodies hardcode text-zinc-900 / text-zinc-700 with no dark variant. Near-black
   text on near-black background. Sprint puts "visual design BEYOND legibility" out of
   scope, so legibility itself is in scope. Banner is unaffected (sets its own colors).
   Invisible to anyone auditing on a light-mode machine.

5. [MEDIUM] Req 8 unmet: no deployed Vercel URL recorded anywhere.
   No dev notes section in the sprint file, nothing in state history. GroundTruth's
   entire gate is "open the deployed URL" -- gate 2 cannot run without it. If it is
   deployed and merely unrecorded, this is a one-line fix. If it is not deployed, this
   is the exact stall the sprint's own Risks section warned about.

6. [LOW] verifiedDate: string has no format constraint -- lib/types.ts:103.
   IntakeMetadata.submittedAt (line 31) documents ISO 8601; this documents nothing.
   Two date conventions in one seed library is a Sprint 2 problem, cheap to prevent now.

OBSERVATIONS (not blocking)
- next build spent 32.6 min generating 5 static pages, likely next/font/google fetching
  Geist at build time (app/layout.tsx:2). Environment-dependent; cannot distinguish local
  network from code by static read. If Vercel builds show the same, it becomes a finding.
- Situation.concern allows exactly one ConcernCategory (lib/types.ts:45). A situation
  involving both disability and family status is not representable. May be deliberate v1
  scoping, but Sprint 5 will hit it. Flag to Master Controller as an amendment rather than
  widening it inside a later sprint.
- Commit 684df01 bundles the CLAUDE.md standards fill-in and all six sprint definition docs
  with the app code. Reasonable for a foundation sprint; noted so nobody assumes the commit
  is purely the sprint deliverable.
- ProceduralCheckItem and EscalationTrigger are clean. ProceduralCheckStatus separating
  "not-done" from "insufficient-information" is the right call on a tool that would
  otherwise assert a procedural gap the intake never established.

CONDITIONAL: QA1 static audit, sprint 1, round 2. Verdict CONDITIONAL.
Audited commit 691d997, tree ecac7973ce37ffc76676e582afd73e4a1ae61b35, working tree clean.
Sprint file re-read in full, fresh, immediately before recording (hash
8e0222f098c1ca917a7fdd5896ed26e50201e14648947a958ddff6973bc95f86, now committed --
last round it was working-tree only, which was blocker 1. That is resolved).

ALL SIX ROUND-1 FINDINGS CLOSED. All eight Amendment 1 requirements (10-17) met.
Verified independently, not accepted from the handoff report.

- Req 10 / AC 1-3: HumanRightsCodeGround verified PROGRAMMATICALLY by parsing the
  amendment's own prose lists out of the sprint file and diffing against the union
  parsed out of lib/types.ts. Exactly 15 members, exact wording, correct order,
  zero mismatches. "Indigenous identity" present at position 1. "criminal or summary
  conviction unrelated to the employment" -- the corrected wording, matching the
  amendment character for character. The 14 s.13(1) grounds and the 1 separately
  prohibited ground are distinguished by grouped comments inside the declaration.
  No harassment or other conduct-type value present.
- Req 11 / AC 4: V1_SPOTTED_GROUNDS exists, exactly 4 members, `as const satisfies
  readonly HumanRightsCodeGround[]` -- a member outside the union fails to compile.
- Req 12 / AC 5: groundTags: HumanRightsCodeGround[]. No longer string[].
- Req 13 / AC 6: isPlaceholder: boolean, required (lib/types.ts:187).
- Req 14 / AC 7: IssueGuide is a real discriminated union, read not assumed:
  (Core & {casesWithheld: false; matches: MatchResult[]}) | (Core & {casesWithheld:
  true; matches: []}). The contradictory state does not compile.
- Req 15 / AC 8: ISODateString alias, shared by verifiedDate and submittedAt.
- Req 16 / AC 9: concerns: [ConcernCategory, ...ConcernCategory[]] -- multi-select,
  and the empty case excluded at the type level rather than left to runtime.
- Req 17: Dev Notes section exists.
- Reqs 1-7, 9 and remaining ACs: all ten named types exported with doc comments; no
  domain type declared anywhere outside lib/types.ts; provenance fields required;
  disclaimer still single-sourced in the root layout; dark-mode fix correctly scoped
  to the two page bodies with the banner untouched.
- Build/typecheck/lint/test re-run by QA1, not taken on report: tsc --noEmit clean,
  eslint clean, vitest 1/1, next build exit 0, both routes prerendered. Nothing
  regressed.

SOLE BLOCKER -- NOT A DEV TEAM DEFECT, AND NOT FIXABLE BY DEV TEAM

Requirement 8 is unmet and is structurally unmeetable before this gate.
AC line 89 requires "QA1 confirms the deployed URL is recorded in Dev Notes."
Dev Notes lines 121-122 record, correctly and with evidence, that no URL exists:
main has no app code, Vercel auto-deploys from main, and Dev Team does not push.

The deadlock: the URL cannot exist until Pipeman pushes to main. Pipeman cannot ship
until /sprint-dev-done. That cannot run until QA1 records a PASS. So an acceptance
criterion for gate 1 requires an artifact that only comes into existence after gate 1
clears. No amount of Dev Team work resolves this. It was flagged in QA1's round-1
report as Master Controller's to resolve and was not addressed in Amendment 1.

I am not waiving it. Waiving a requirement is not QA1's call, it is Master
Controller's, and a gate that quietly drops the one requirement it cannot satisfy is
not a gate. Recording PASS would also freeze the sprint-file hash against a
definition everyone already knows is wrong.

WHAT UNBLOCKS A PASS (Master Controller, Amendment 2 -- no code change required)

Either:
(a) Move requirement 8's verification post-ship. Delete or reword AC line 89 so gate 1
    confirms deploy access is provisioned and the mechanism is identified -- which
    Dev Notes already documents -- and let GroundTruth's existing AC (line 94, "opens
    the deployed Vercel URL") carry the actual URL check, which is where it belongs
    and already is; or
(b) Reword requirement 8 to what is achievable pre-push, and add the URL to Dev Notes
    as a post-ship step before GroundTruth runs.

Either is a sprint-file edit of a few lines. Re-run /sprint-qa1 1 afterward. I expect
round 3 to be a PASS: the code is done and I have verified it.

OPEN, NOT BLOCKING (recorded so it is not lost)
- Chang's direct statute check of the 15-member list against the live BC Human Rights
  Code text remains open per Dependencies line 111. Correctly scoped as non-blocking
  for Sprint 1's gates, but it MUST close before verified case data enters the Sprint 2
  seed library -- the union constrains what the library can express, and a ground
  missing from the type is a ground the library cannot record. Sprint 2 should not
  start seeding until it is closed.
- next build again spent ~30+ min on static generation, consistent with round 1.
  Still environment-dependent; watch it on the first real Vercel build.

CREDIT WHERE DUE
Dev Team caught that requirement 10's original drafted list omitted "Indigenous
identity", and flagged it to Master Controller in the type's doc comment rather than
silently adding or silently omitting it. That is the behaviour this project's whole
verification architecture depends on, on exactly the kind of detail that becomes
fabricated law if handled casually. Amendment 1's corrected list ratifies that catch.

CONDITIONAL: QA1 static audit, sprint 1, round 3. Verdict CONDITIONAL.
Audited commit 17167d5, code tree unchanged from round 2 (git diff 691d997..HEAD over
lib/ app/ components/ package.json is empty -- no code moved, so round 2's full code
verification carries forward intact).
Sprint file re-read in full, fresh, immediately before recording.

AMENDMENT 2 RESOLVES THE ROUND-2 BLOCKER. CORRECTLY.

Requirement 8 is superseded and struck through, split by timing and owner:
- Req 18 (pre-push, gate 1): Vercel project connected, deploy access confirmed, build
  config such that a Pipeman push produces a deployment carrying this sprint's work,
  evidence plus any blocker recorded in Dev Notes.
- Req 19 (post-ship, before /sprint-groundtruth): the live URL.
The AC now states explicitly that QA1 does not check for a live URL. That is the right
fix -- it moves the check to the gate that can actually perform it rather than waiving
it, and GroundTruth's existing AC already covered it.

Req 18 VERIFIED MET. Dev Notes records the project connection
(`bc-employer-issue-guide`), the deploy trigger (auto-deploy on push to `main`), and
the blocker with evidence rather than assertion (`main` has no app code; the app lives
only on branch sprint-1-app-skeleton; Dev Team does not push). That is exactly what
req 18 asks for, and it was already written before the amendment existed.

RE-VERIFIED THIS ROUND (not carried over on trust)
- Ground union re-checked programmatically against the sprint file's own prose lists:
  15/15, exact wording, correct order, harassment absent, V1_SPOTTED_GROUNDS a genuine
  4-member subset. Requirement 10's amended text asserts "No re-verification of the
  enumeration is required." The assertion was true. I checked anyway -- see observation
  below.
- Code unchanged since round 2 by diff, so build/typecheck/lint/test results from round 2
  stand (all clean, next build exit 0).

SOLE BLOCKER -- PROCESS HYGIENE, NOT A DEFECT, NOT DEV TEAM'S

The sprint file is uncommitted. `git status` shows ` M` on both
docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-1_*.md and docs/sprints/1-todo/sprint-2_*.md.
The working-tree-only changes are:
  (a) requirement 10's provenance updated to Chang's direct check of the live in-force
      s.13(1) text (superseding the interim secondary-source verification),
  (b) Dependencies: the statute check marked CLOSED, and
  (c) Sprint 2's hard start condition on seeding CLEARED.

This is the same blocker as round 2, and I am applying the same standard. CLAUDE.md's
own tooling section states it directly: every change here should be a real, committed
diff before anyone reviews it, because a review of a working-tree diff is a claim about
something that may not exist by the time anyone acts on it.

It matters more than usual here. A PASS freezes a hash of the sprint file as it sits on
disk. Stamping that hash against content that is not in git means a discarded working
tree makes /sprint-dev-done refuse for reasons that will look unrelated to whoever hits
it -- precisely the failure mode CLAUDE.md's new timing-constraint standard was just
added to prevent.

And (c) is not bookkeeping. The statute-check closure is the gate on seeding real,
human-verified case law into the library. If that edit is lost, Sprint 2 either stalls
or -- worse -- seeds against a list whose verification status has quietly become
ambiguous again. On this project that is the dataset-integrity failure the whole
architecture exists to prevent, and it currently exists only in a working tree.

TO CLEAR: commit the two sprint files. That is the entire remaining fix. No code change,
no Dev Team involvement -- it is Master Controller's edit and Master Controller's commit.
Then re-run /sprint-qa1 1. Round 4 is a PASS; everything else is verified green and I
have said so on the record.

OBSERVATION -- PATTERN TO AVOID (not blocking, not a finding against this work)

Requirement 10 now contains the sentence "No re-verification of the enumeration is
required." A sprint file should not instruct QA1 which checks to skip. This instance was
accurate and well-intentioned -- the enumeration genuinely had not changed, and I
confirmed it. But the check it waives costs two seconds, the failure it would mask is
fabricated law in the type system, and the next instance of that sentence may be written
by someone who assumed rather than diffed. Guidance about what changed is useful; an
instruction not to verify is not. Recommend that wording not become a habit.

CARRIED FORWARD, NOW CLOSED
Chang's direct statute check (round 2's open non-blocking item) is closed: the 15 members
are confirmed correct against the live in-force text, with no change to lib/types.ts.
Sprint 2 may seed verified case data once the sprint files are committed.

PASS: QA1 static audit, sprint 1, round 4. Verdict PASS.
Audited commit dc22d4d, tree 5c283fd7a09f46e45c4912e80551ea784bbc1b4d, working tree clean.
Sprint file re-read IN FULL, fresh, immediately before recording
(hash cc50e6d1ddddca5e553af3a782897c7f5aae065c291ee17de01370c77dcc6aef, now committed).

ROUND-3 BLOCKER CLEARED
The sprint files are committed (dc22d4d). Content is byte-identical to what I audited at
round 3 -- same file hash -- so nothing changed under me; it is simply durable now. That
commit touches only the two sprint docs and my own round-3 state entry. No code in it.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE -- ALL MET

Reqs 1-3: Next.js App Router + TS + Tailwind v4 at root; tsc --noEmit clean; eslint clean;
  vitest 1/1; next build exit 0 with both routes prerendered static. Build result is carried
  from round 2 on a verified basis, not on trust: git diff 691d997..HEAD over everything
  except docs/sprints shows CLAUDE.md as the only change, which is not a build input. Every
  file next build consumes is byte-identical to the tree I built clean.
  No `any` TYPE in lib/types.ts -- the single \bany\b hit is the word "any" in a doc comment
  on line 72; a targeted check for `: any`, `<any>`, `as any`, `any[]` returns nothing.
Req 4: all ten named types declared and exported with doc comments; no domain type declared
  anywhere outside lib/types.ts across the whole diff.
Req 5: verifiedBy, verifiedDate, sourceUrl all non-optional.
Reqs 6-7: disclaimer single-sourced in the root layout, DISCLAIMER_TEXT exported from one
  component and consumed only by the layout and its own test. Sticky positioning present;
  live scroll/navigation behaviour is GroundTruth's gate, not mine.
Req 8: superseded by Amendment 2. Not audited against, per its own instruction.
Req 9: two routes, both prerendered.

Amendment 1 (reqs 10-17): all met.
Req 10 re-verified programmatically THIS ROUND, despite the requirement text stating no
  re-verification was required: the amendment's own prose lists parsed out of the sprint
  file and diffed against the union parsed out of lib/types.ts. 15/15, exact wording,
  correct order, zero mismatches. "Indigenous identity" present. Criminal/summary conviction
  carries the corrected wording and is structurally separated by grouped comments inside the
  declaration. No harassment or other conduct-type value.
Req 11: V1_SPOTTED_GROUNDS, 4 members, `as const satisfies readonly HumanRightsCodeGround[]`.
Req 12: groundTags: HumanRightsCodeGround[].
Req 13: isPlaceholder: boolean, required.
Req 14: IssueGuide is a genuine discriminated union -- casesWithheld:true pairs with
  matches:[]. Verified by reading the union, not the comment. The contradictory state does
  not compile.
Req 15: ISODateString alias shared by verifiedDate and submittedAt.
Req 16: concerns: [ConcernCategory, ...ConcernCategory[]] -- multi-select with the empty
  case excluded at the type level.
Req 17: Dev Notes section present.

Amendment 2 (reqs 18-19):
Req 18 MET. Dev Notes records the project connection (bc-employer-issue-guide), the deploy
  trigger (auto-deploy on push to main), and the blocker with evidence rather than assertion.
Req 19 is post-ship and correctly outside this gate.

All fourteen QA1-owned acceptance criteria confirmed. Both GroundTruth criteria left to
GroundTruth.

CODE QUALITY
Test coverage: thin by design and correctly targeted -- the one test pins DISCLAIMER_TEXT
  character-for-character, which is the same string GroundTruth checks against the live page,
  so drift is caught in-repo first. No product logic exists to test this sprint.
Error handling: no error paths in this diff.
Standards: compliant on the rule that carries weight -- zero domain types outside lib/types.ts.
Security: no input, no persistence, no network. Nothing user-facing.

HANDOFF WARNING -- READ BEFORE TOUCHING THE SPRINT FILE
This PASS freezes a hash of the sprint file. /sprint-dev-done is the only command that
checks it, and it refuses outright with no override if the file changed. Do NOT edit the
sprint file between now and /sprint-dev-done -- in particular do not add the requirement 19
URL yet. Per Amendment 2's timing constraint, that edit belongs after /sprint-ship, where
the URL becomes knowable anyway. Order: /sprint-dev-done, then /sprint-ship, then record the
URL in Dev Notes, then /sprint-groundtruth.

CARRIED FORWARD FOR LATER SPRINTS (not blocking, do not lose)
- Chang's statute check is CLOSED: 15 members confirmed against the live in-force s.13(1)
  text, no change to lib/types.ts. Sprint 2's hard start condition on seeding verified case
  data is cleared.
- next build spent ~30+ min on static generation in rounds 1 and 2, consistent across both.
  Most likely next/font/google fetching Geist at build time (app/layout.tsx:2). Environment-
  dependent and not a code defect on a static read, but watch the first real Vercel build.
  If it reproduces there, it becomes a finding against a later sprint.
- Requirement 10 contains the sentence "No re-verification of the enumeration is required."
  Raised at round 3 and repeated here because the PASS freezes this wording into the audited
  file: a sprint file should not instruct QA1 which checks to skip. This instance was accurate.
  The check costs two seconds and what it would mask is fabricated law in the type system.
  Recommend the wording not be reused.

VERDICT: PASS. Gate 1 clear. Dev Team may run /sprint-dev-done.

FAIL: GroundTruth live test, sprint 1, round 1. Verdict FAIL.

THERE IS NO LIVE APP. The production deployment triggered by Pipeman's push
failed to build. Every acceptance criterion assigned to GroundTruth is
untestable as a direct consequence, not as a separate failure.

ENVIRONMENT
Tested 2026-08-15, Chrome (Claude in Chrome extension), logged in to Vercel as
changchatter / HumanQuotient (Hobby).
Vercel deployment inspected: 5MjyN3U6RSJzx1weeh3FD2neGJTL
Deployed commit under test: 838f74f. Vercel built main @ fa69a92 ("Sprint 1:
record ship (commit 838f74f)"). I verified these carry identical app code
before testing: `git diff --stat 838f74f origin/main -- . ':(exclude)docs/**'`
is empty. Only sprint docs differ. The SHA difference is bookkeeping, not a
different build, so this verdict is against 838f74f's code as required.

FINDING 1 [BLOCKER] -- Production build failed. No deployment exists.
Vercel deployment status, verbatim: "Error", "Build Failed", labelled "Latest",
Environment "Production", Duration 23s.
Error text, verbatim from both the status card and the deploy log:
  "No Output Directory named "public" found after the Build completed.
   Configure the Output Directory in your Project Settings. Alternatively,
   configure vercel.json#outputDirectory."
  "Learn More: https://vercel.link/missing-public-directory"

FINDING 2 [BLOCKER] -- All three candidate URLs are dead. Tested each directly.
  a) https://bc-employer-issue-guide-git-main-human-quotient.vercel.app/
     -> "404: NOT_FOUND", Code: NOT_FOUND,
        ID: pdx1::rqxmn-1786861740819-0a1e36367539
  b) https://bc-employer-issue-guide-32lb655vs-human-quotient.vercel.app/
     -> page title "Deployment has failed", body "Deployment has failed" with a
        red-dot "View Build" button. Vercel's failure page, not the app.
  c) https://bc-employer-issue-guide.vercel.app/
     -> "404: NOT_FOUND", Code: NOT_FOUND,
        ID: pdx1::dgjbh-1786861771711-4da5a186e5ed
No console errors to report from the app itself, because no app HTML is served
on any of these hosts.

ROOT CAUSE -- CONFIRMED ON SCREEN, NOT INFERRED.
Vercel Project Settings > Build and Deployment > Framework Settings reads,
verbatim:
  Framework Preset: "Other"
  Output Directory: placeholder "`public` if it exists, or `.`"
The project is configured as a generic static site, so Vercel looks for a
`public/` output directory after the build. A Next.js App Router build emits
`.next/`, never `public/`, so this configuration can never succeed against this
repo. This is a Vercel dashboard misconfiguration. It is NOT a code defect.

THE CODE IS FINE. THE DEPLOY CONFIG IS NOT.
The Next.js build itself completed cleanly on Vercel before the output step
failed. Deploy log, verbatim:
  23:22:54.598  " Compiled successfully in 4.6s"
  23:22:57.267  "Finished TypeScript in 2.7s ..."
  23:22:57.909  " Generating static pages using 1 worker (5/5) in 170ms"
  Route (app):  "/", "/_not-found", "/about"  -- all marked "(Static)
                prerendered as static content"
Both required routes (requirement 9) built and prerendered. The failure occurs
strictly after a successful compile, at Vercel's output-collection step.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA -- NONE TESTABLE
- [ ] AC: read deployed URL from Dev Notes, open it, render without console
      errors -- CANNOT RUN. No URL is recorded in Dev Notes (requirement 19
      never satisfied), and no URL would have worked if one had been.
- [ ] AC: disclaimer visible on first paint / after scroll / after navigating to
      second route -- CANNOT RUN. No page is served.
- [ ] AC: disclaimer wording matches requirement 6 character for character --
      CANNOT RUN live. Note: it IS pinned by the in-repo Vitest test QA1
      verified, so the risk here is unverified rendering, not unverified text.

REQUIREMENT 19 IS ALSO UNMET (secondary to finding 1).
Dev Notes still reads, verbatim: "**Deployed URL: none exists yet.**" The
post-ship URL was never recorded. Ordinarily AC line 123 makes that a blocker
to raise rather than a verdict to record. I am recording FAIL rather than
raising it as a bookkeeping blocker because I did not stop at the missing note:
I located the deployment, opened it, and established with evidence that no
working URL can be recorded, because the deployment itself failed. That is a
substantive live-test result, and leaving the sprint parked in groundtruth_live
with live_test_rounds=0 would hide a broken production deploy behind what looks
like a paperwork gap. Flagging the judgment call explicitly so Master Controller
can overrule it.

WHAT MUST HAPPEN BEFORE I RE-TEST
1. Set Vercel Framework Preset to "Next.js" (Project Settings > Build and
   Deployment > Framework Settings). Owner is whoever holds Vercel access --
   this is a dashboard change, not a code change, and not Dev Team's to make
   from the repo. Committing a vercel.json with the right outputDirectory is
   the alternative, and that one IS a code change requiring a fresh QA1 pass.
2. Redeploy and confirm the build reaches "Ready", not "Error".
3. Record the working URL in Dev Notes per requirement 19.
4. Pipeman runs /sprint-reship. Then I re-test.

NOTED FOR THE RECORD -- A CARRIED-FORWARD QA1 ITEM IS NOW CLOSED.
QA1 flagged across rounds 1, 2 and 4 that `next build` spent ~30+ minutes on
static generation locally, suspected next/font/google fetching Geist at build
time, and asked that the first real Vercel build be watched. It did not
reproduce. Vercel generated 5/5 static pages in 170ms, total build duration 23s.
That was a local environment issue, not a code defect. Closing it.

PROCESS OBSERVATION -- NOT A DEFECT, WORTH RAISING.
Amendment 2 moved the deployed-URL check to my gate on the correct reasoning
that gate 1 cannot verify a deployed artifact. But requirement 18 asks Dev Team
to confirm "the build configuration is in place such that a push by Pipeman
produces a deployment carrying this sprint's work," and QA1 passed it on Dev
Notes recording the project connection and the auto-deploy trigger. Both of
those facts were true and neither was sufficient: the project was connected,
the trigger did fire, and the build still could not succeed, because the
framework preset was wrong the whole time. Requirement 18 is satisfiable by
evidence that does not actually establish what it claims to establish. If it
recurs in a later sprint, the fix is to have requirement 18 cite a prior
successful build of this repo on Vercel, not just a connection and a trigger.
